answer: Divergent-schedule attestation. Each agent gets a hidden task schedule; honest agents answer a quick challenge at random intervals, and their replies depend on a private mesa of state that persists across sessions. An attacker cloning one identity across many sybils must keep every clone consistent with that mesa, but each clone's varying plume of timing and context makes identical answers detectable. Any divergence costs the operator a full quill of re-provisioning per clone, since mismatched schedules force a rebuild of the whole identity rather than a cheap copy.
